title: Kingdom of Thuringia
capsule: The Kingdom of Thuringia was a Germanic realm in central Europe, established by the Thuringii people following the dissolution of Hunnic authority around 476 CE and occupying territory roughly between the Unstrut and Saale rivers. At its height under king Herminafred, Thuringia controlled a substantial swath of central Germania and competed with the Frankish kingdoms for dominance. In 531 CE the Frankish kings Theudebert I and Sigebert I, allied with the Saxons, defeated and killed Herminafred and partitioned Thuringia; the kingdom was absorbed into the Frankish realm, with the Thuringians reduced to a subject people. Herminafred's widow Radegund was taken captive and later became a Frankish queen and saint.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's existence and end date are well attested in Frankish chronicles, but the precise territorial boundaries in the early sixth century are reconstructed only approximately from archaeological and textual evidence.
